questions.q: What was the secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact?
questions.answer: The secret protocol divided Romania, Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Finland into German and Soviet spheres of influence.

questions.q: Which countries were assigned to the Soviet sphere of influence in the north according to the secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact?
questions.answer: Finland, Estonia and Latvia were assigned to the Soviet sphere.

questions.q: How was Poland to be partitioned according to the secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact?
questions.answer: Poland was to be partitioned in the event of its political rearrangement, with areas east of the Pisa, Narev, Vistula and San rivers going to the Soviet Union while Germany would occupy the west.

triples.o: Pisa, Narev, Vistula and San rivers

questions.q: Which country was reassigned to the Soviet sphere of influence by a second secret protocol in September 1939?

questions.q: What city was Lithuania granted according to the secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact?
questions.answer: Lithuania was granted the city of Vilnius, its historical capital.

questions.q: What was the result of the clause in the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact regarding Bessarabia?
questions.answer: Bessarabia was joined to the Moldovan ASSR and became the Moldovan SSR under control of Moscow.

triples.o: Bessarabia joined to Moldovan ASSR and became Moldovan SSR

triples.o: sands and clays deposited on decaying organic marine matter

questions.q: What formations were created by the upward movement of salt in Houston?

questions.q: What is trial division?
questions.answer: The most basic method of checking the primality of a given integer n, consisting of dividing n by each integer m greater than 1 and less than or equal to the square root of n.

questions.q: What is the condition for an integer n to be prime using trial division?
questions.answer: If none of the divisions by integers m greater than 1 and less than or equal to the square root of n yields an integer, then n is prime.

triples.o: if no division by m (1 < m ≤ √n) yields an integer, then n is prime

questions.q: Is 37 prime?
questions.answer: Yes, 37 is prime because none of 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 divides it.

questions.answer: The Australian Capital Territory has a unicameral parliament.

questions.q: What is the upper house of a state parliament called?
questions.answer: The upper houses are known as the Legislative Council.

questions.q: Who is the head of government in each Australian state?
questions.answer: The head of the government in each state is the Premier.

questions.q: Who is the head of government in each Australian territory?
questions.answer: The head of the government in each territory is the Chief Minister.

questions.q: Who represents the Queen in each Australian state?
questions.answer: The Queen is represented in each state by a governor.

questions.q: Who represents the Queen in the Northern Territory?
questions.answer: In the Northern Territory, the Queen is represented by the Administrator.

questions.q: Who represents the Queen in the Commonwealth of Australia?
questions.answer: In the Commonwealth, the Queen's representative is the Governor-General.

questions.q: Which external territories are directly administered by the Commonwealth Parliament?
questions.answer: The Commonwealth Parliament directly administers Ashmore and Cartier Islands, Australian Antarctic Territory, Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Coral Sea Islands, Heard Island and McDonald Islands, and Jervis Bay Territory.

questions.q: What is Jervis Bay Territory?
questions.answer: Jervis Bay Territory is a naval base and sea port for the national capital in land that was formerly part of New South Wales.

questions.q: What was Norfolk Island's autonomy under the Norfolk Island Act 1979?
questions.answer: The external territory of Norfolk Island previously exercised considerable autonomy under the Norfolk Island Act 1979 through its own legislative assembly and an Administrator to represent the Queen.

questions.q: What happened to Norfolk Island's self-government in 2015?
questions.answer: In 2015, the Commonwealth Parliament abolished self-government, integrating Norfolk Island into the Australian tax and welfare systems and replacing its legislative assembly with a council.

questions.answer: It is a sturdy, muscular, compact dog that gives the impression of agility and strength, with a broad skull, muscular cheeks, a medium-length deep powerful muzzle, pricked ears, oval dark eyes, strong muscular neck and shoulders, straight parallel forelegs, and round arched feet.

questions.q: What does the Australian Cattle Dog's breed standard say about its muscles?
questions.answer: The breed standard states it should have well-conditioned muscles, even when bred for companion or show purposes.

questions.q: What should the Australian Cattle Dog's appearance be like according to its breed standard?
questions.answer: Its appearance should be symmetrical and balanced, with no individual part exaggerated, and it should not look delicate or cumbersome.

questions.q: Why should the Australian Cattle Dog not look delicate or cumbersome?
questions.answer: Because either characteristic limits the agility and endurance necessary for a working dog.

title: Hemostasis

questions.q: What is hemostasis?
questions.answer: Hemostasis is the instinctive response for the body to stop bleeding and loss of blood when blood is present outside of the body or blood vessels.

triples.o: the instinctive response for the body to stop bleeding and loss of blood

questions.q: What are the three steps of hemostasis in order?
questions.answer: Vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, and coagulation (blood clotting).

questions.q: What is vascular spasm?
questions.answer: Vascular spasm is the first response in hemostasis where blood vessels constrict to allow less blood to be lost.

triples.o: the first response as the blood vessels constrict to allow less blood to be lost

questions.q: What is platelet plug formation?
questions.answer: Platelet plug formation is the second step of hemostasis where platelets stick together to form a temporary seal to cover the break in the vessel wall.

triples.o: platelets stick together to form a temporary seal to cover the break in the vessel wall

questions.q: What is coagulation?
questions.answer: Coagulation, or blood clotting, is the third and last step of hemostasis that reinforces the platelet plug with fibrin threads that act as a molecular glue.

triples.o: reinforces the platelet plug with fibrin threads that act as a molecular glue

questions.q: What is the role of platelets in hemostasis?
questions.answer: Platelets are a large factor in the hemostatic process; they allow for the creation of the platelet plug that forms almost directly after a blood vessel has been ruptured.

triples.o: allow for the creation of the platelet plug that forms almost directly after a blood vessel has been ruptured
